summary:
Project Idea & Objective

An innovative digital system designed to monitor and track ground subsidence, uplift, and surface deformations in Jeddah using remote sensing technologies and space-borne radar data.

Technologies & Data Used

Data Sources: Leveraging real radar data from the Sentinel-1 satellite (SAR & InSAR) via NASA's ASF Vertex platform.

Data Processing & Analysis: Utilizing ESA SNAP software, Geographic Information Systems (QGIS), and Google Earth Engine to process radar images and extract surface displacement measurements.

Programming & Interface Development: Building the prototype using Python (utilizing libraries such as Rasterio, NumPy, Pandas, and Folium) and designing an interactive interface for data and map visualization via Streamlit.

Project Value Added

The system enables the early detection of geological and surface changes in Jeddah's infrastructure and soil, supporting decision-making in urban planning and mitigating environmental and engineering risks based on accurate and reliable space data.

Technical Innovation Report
Jeddah Ground Deformation Monitoring System (Subsidence, Uplift, and Surface Changes)
1. Project Introduction
Jeddah is one of the most vital economic and strategic cities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Due to rapid urban expansion, hydrogeological changes, and groundwater extraction, the city is vulnerable to ground surface deformations such as subsidence and uplift. This project introduces an innovative digital monitoring system utilizing advanced space technologies to detect these changes with high precision, supporting sustainable urban planning.
2. Project Objectives
Early Detection: Monitor minute surface changes (at millimeter scales) before they escalate into engineering or environmental hazards.
Leveraging Open Data: Utilize free, high-resolution radar data (Sentinel-1) to provide cost-effective and sustainable solutions.
Decision Support: Build an interactive web platform enabling engineers and urban planners to seamlessly visualize geological maps and data.
3. Data Sources & Methodology
The system relies on an integrated scientific workflow consisting of the following stages:
Data Acquisition:
Utilizing Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data from the Sentinel-1 satellite constellation (European Space Agency - ESA).
Downloading and managing data via NASA's ASF Vertex platform.
Processing & Analysis (InSAR Analysis):
Using ESA SNAP software to apply Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (DInSAR) techniques for extracting surface displacement maps.
Employing Google Earth Engine (GEE) and QGIS for spatial analysis and mapping geospatial data over Jeddah.
Software Development & Dashboard:
Developing core algorithms and data processing pipelines in Python using libraries such as Rasterio, NumPy, and Pandas.
Integrating interactive mapping components using Folium.
Designing a full-featured, user-friendly interactive web dashboard using Streamlit.
4. Value Added & Practical Applications
Infrastructure Protection: Monitoring the impact of ground deformation on roads, bridges, sewage networks, and residential buildings.
Urban Risk Management: Assisting municipalities and urban planning authorities in identifying subsidence-prone areas to enforce necessary engineering precautions.
Technical Sustainability: Delivering a scalable prototype ready for future integration with smart city frameworks.
